labelled with ""sequence identifiers"" in order to prevent the server from
reordering RPC requests
column2: as this could cause its file state to

column1: become out of sync with the client.
Currently the NFS client code enforces this ordering locally using
semaphores to restrict access to structures until the RPC call is done.
This
column3: only works with synchronous RPC calls

column1: user process must first grab the semaphore.
By dropping semaphores
column2: and instead teaching the RPC engine to hold

column1: the RPC calls until they are ready to be sent
process to work nicely with asynchronous RPC calls too.
This patch adds a new list called ""rpc_sequence"" that defines the order
of the RPC calls to be sent. We add one such list for each state_owner.
When an RPC call is ready to be sent
column2: it checks if it is top of the

column1: rpc_sequence list. If so
and loops until it hits top of the list.
Once the RPC call has completed
column2: it can then bump the sequence id counter

column1: and remove itself from the rpc_sequence list
column2: and then wake up the next

column1: sleeper.
Note that the state_owner sequence ids and lock_owner sequence ids are
all indexed to the same rpc_sequence list
